practices.practice: Store the Azure DocumentDB connection string in an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and read it at runtime rather than committing credentials to source control.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB mongoose connect MONGODB_URI don't commit

practices.practice: Open and reuse a single MongoDB/Mongoose connection (singleton MongoClient) across the app rather than creating a new connection per request; tune connection options (dbName, maxIdleTimeMS, retryWrites as appropriate) at connect time.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB mongoose connection reuse maxIdleTimeMS

practices.practice: Set driver-level retryWrites cautiously and prefer application-level bounded retries with idempotency safeguards for non‑idempotent writes; the quickstart shows retryWrites=false and explains why blindly retrying writes is risky.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB retryWrites application retries guidance

practices.practice: Use Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC) and Azure RBAC or native database users as appropriate; support for Entra ID lets you avoid storing long-lived DB passwords and enables least-privilege access control.
practices.source_name: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID (azure-portal)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB Microsoft Entra ID RBAC authentication

practices.practice: Use TLS and the mongodb+srv scheme in your connection URI and include recommended client options such as tls=true, authMechanism (SCRAM-SHA-256 or MONGODB-OIDC), retryWrites=false, and maxIdleTimeMS when connecting.
practices.source_name: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID (azure-resource-manager-bicep)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB connection string tls=true retrywrites=false maxIdleTimeMS

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB supports TTL functionality; you can use collection TTL (system _ts-based TTL) and per-document TTL semantics (document 'ttl' field) to expire data automatically — follow the service's TTL examples and constraints.
practices.source_name: Expire data with Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB and per-document TTL
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB TTL index per-document ttl 'ttl' property

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB supports the common MongoDB index types (single-field, compound, multikey, text, wildcard, hashed, geospatial) and also vector indexes; be aware that building a unique index may block operations during the build.
practices.source_name: MongoDB Query Language (MQL) compatibility in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB index types supported hashed wildcard vector index

practices.practice: When using vector search, choose the right index algorithm (IVF/HNSW/DiskANN) for workload size and tune index/query parameters (numLists for IVF, efConstruction/M for HNSW, lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree for DiskANN) and pick cluster tier (M30+ for DiskANN/HNSW) based on scale.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index DiskANN HNSW IVF tuning efSearch efConstruction lBuild

practices.practice: Pre-filter non-vector predicates (tenantId, date ranges, metadata) before running vector search so the vector engine only scores a small candidate set and preserves top-k recall and performance.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB pre-filter vector search candidate set

practices.practice: Index builds may block operations for certain index types (notably unique indexes) and some index features have limits; prefer creating needed indexes explicitly at startup and monitor index-build progress when migrating or creating indexes on large collections.
practices.source_name: Manage indexing in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB unique index build blocks advice

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and integrate Azure DocumentDB with Azure Monitor / Log Analytics for slow-query logs, resource metrics (CPU/memory/IOPS), and alerts on saturation or throttling.
practices.source_name: Reliability in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB monitor diagnostic settings slow query logs Azure Monitor

practices.practice: Provision the appropriate compute tier and storage for your workload (DocumentDB uses vCore/cluster tiers like M30 rather than RU/s); choose M30+ for production vector workloads and scale compute independently from storage.
practices.source_name: What is Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)?
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB provision compute tiers M30 vCore storage decoupled

practices.practice: Use Private Link / private endpoints and firewall rules to restrict network access to clusters and avoid enabling public access; prefer Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities for service-to-service auth where possible.
practices.source_name: What is Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)?
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB Private Link firewall Microsoft Entra ID authentication

practices.practice: Avoid storing large binary blobs in DocumentDB; store large objects in Azure Blob Storage and keep only metadata/references in the database to keep documents small and indexable.
practices.source_name: Introduction to Azure Blob Storage
practices.how_found: store large objects blob storage vs database guidance

practices.practice: Cache-aside is a recommended pattern for application-level caches: on read check cache, on miss fetch from origin, update cache, and plan TTLs and eviction policies according to access patterns.
practices.source_name: Cache-Aside pattern
practices.how_found: Cache-Aside pattern stale-while-revalidate general guidance

practices.practice: Ensure query predicates (tenantId, key lookups, date ranges) are covered by indexes to avoid collection scans; use explain("executionStats") to validate index usage.
practices.source_name: Scenario based guide to indexing in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB explain executionStats avoid COLLSCAN index usage

practices.practice: When creating vector indexes, vectors must be number[] and only one vector per path may be indexed; non-number types prevent indexing and documents without indexed vectors won't appear in vector-search results.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vectors must be number[] to be indexed

practices.practice: Use Azure-provided tooling and migration assessment (DocumentDB migration extension) to check feature compatibility before migrating MongoDB workloads to Azure DocumentDB.
practices.source_name: Migrate MongoDB to Azure DocumentDB online by using Azure DocumentDB migration extension
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB migration assessment extension compatibility

practices.practice: Use Azure Monitor / diagnostic settings to alert on throttling, connection pool exhaustion, and other resource saturation metrics rather than relying on client-side errors alone.
practices.source_name: Reliability in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB monitor alerts throttling IOPS CPU connection saturation

practices.practice: When using Mongoose or drivers, percent-encode reserved characters in usernames/passwords before putting them in a URI and do not percent-encode the entire URI; use `.env` and avoid printing URIs or credentials.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: percent-encode username password mongodb uri azure documentdb

practices.practice: Create indexes explicitly at startup rather than relying on automatic background creation and test index behavior (unique indexes, wildcard, text index limits) against your target cluster and tier.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB disable automatic index creation create indexes explicitly

practices.practice: For vector workloads at production scale, prefer DiskANN on M30+ clusters as the default algorithm due to better scaling and higher supported embedding dimensions; reserve HNSW for max-recall scenarios and IVF for small/dev datasets.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Vector index with TypeScript in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB choose DiskANN HNSW IVF recommendations M30
